Rework does not flip the decision. I measured 283 real recycle pairs. On the policy-like recycles (idle at least 15 minutes, 150k to 350k tokens) the rework costs about 0.7 pp/week, against a saving of 16 to 20 pp/week.

How I measured it: all 4 accounts, files touched from 2026-09-24 on. 302 sessions open with a brief carrying a HANDOFF-RECYCLE marker, so they are successors. In 292 the brief itself names the predecessor, and 283 pairs were usable. A 'turn' here is one assistant API request. Token counts are estimates (tool-result characters / 4). Costs are priced at your weights and scaled to 155 recycles a week (310 per 14 days). A repeated result is charged one cache write and then a read on every later successor request.

Measured cost, from three definitions (the first 10 successor requests against the predecessor's last 50, unless stated):
- **Your exact definition** (same Read path, same Bash command, same Grep/Glob): 361 tokens per recycle on average (median 0). That is **0.12 pp/week** (90% interval 0.09 to 0.16).
- **Looser file-touch definition** (any call that touches a file the predecessor touched, or reads the predecessor's own transcript): 3.7k tokens per recycle, **1.25 pp/week** (1.10 to 1.41).
  - Fresh sessions in the same folders show 0.34, so the part caused by recycling is about 0.9.
  - The recycles most like the proposed policy (idle at least 15 minutes, predecessor at 150k to 350k, 44 pairs) cost 0.73.
  - With a wider window (first 30 vs last 200) it rises to 2.65 pp/week, or 1.86 if the successor is itself recycled at its next idle point.
- **Upper bound** (every result and request in the first 10 counted as rework): **3.33 pp/week**. Fresh sessions cost 2.95 on the same measure, so successors do no more early work than any new session.

Quality signals:
- The raw tool-error rate is higher in successors: 4.2 per 100 requests, against 1.4 in the predecessor's last 10 and 9.8 in fresh sessions.
- But 84 of the 116 successor errors are 'Exit code 1' on combined read commands that still printed their output.
- Real errors: successors 0.47 per 100 requests, predecessors 0.75, fresh sessions 0.94.
- No edit was undone. The 4 revert-like commands were all `git stash list` reads.
- Phrases like "I don't have context" are essentially absent in every group (at most 0.11 per 100 requests).

A separate correction to the simulation: successors start at a median 78.4k tokens, not the 58.6k it assumed. Its own 'p90 re-prime' row (about 79.7k) gives **16.35 pp/week**, so that is the realistic starting figure. The net saving is then about 15.1 pp/week centrally (16.35 − 1.25), about 13.7 with the wide window, and at least 13.0 at the upper bound.

Limits:
- These were deliberate self-recycles with briefs written by the predecessor, at a median 439k tokens. Recycles forced by an idle timer could land mid-task with weaker briefs.
- Subagent and Workflow runs are not priced. Successors launch 0.67 per session in their first 30 requests, against 0.25 for fresh sessions.
- The cost when the operator returns to a recycled pane (part b) was not measured.

Conviction: 80% that rework leaves the policy at least 12 pp/week ahead.
- It would go down if the first real idle recycles show a median file-touch rework above about 10k tokens per recycle (about 3.4 pp/week). It would also go down if they show subagents or long test and benchmark runs repeating the predecessor's work.
- It would go up if a brief that lists the predecessor's recent files brings file-touch rework close to the fresh-session level.

Everything (scripts, outputs, data) is in /tmp/idle-recycle-risk/a-rework/.

MEASURED (b). Each number comes from a script under /tmp/idle-recycle-risk/b/ (run there, python3 -I). The w4 files are not in this worktree, so I read them from the main checkout, ~/Development/claude-infrastructure/docs/research/usage-levers-2026-10-23/w4/. The row files in /tmp/usage-audit/w4/ are still present.

1) RECYCLE POINTS. points.py reuses sim.py's own sessions, busy() and fire logic, and reproduces W4 exactly: 310 points mid-session plus 218 panes that never resume (terminal), across 199 sessions.
- The idle gap was ended by a MACHINE event at 219 points (71%):
  - 130 background-job or watcher notices
  - 31 peer or teammate messages
  - 23 goal check-ins
  - 15 peer-mail notices
  - 12 restore / limit-recover / crash prompts
  - 8 peer-wakes with no user record
- It was ended by the OPERATOR at 83 points (27%).
- 8 points cannot be checked: their transcript file was deleted after the scan.
- What matters is the operator's first prompt to the successor. 193 points (62%) get one at or after idle minute 15: 80 as the prompt that ends the gap, 113 only after machine turns the successor would already have handled. 114 points get no operator prompt before the session ends. At 3 more points the operator was active before minute 15 (bash-mode commands or a prompt the session never answered).
- The 193 returns are 132 typed prose, 42 bash-mode '!' commands the agent handed over, and 19 slash commands.

2) CONTEXT DEPENDENCE. I labelled 60 random returns by hand (seed 20261024), then reviewed the other 133 as a holdout. Labels:
- H: needs the predecessor's conversation (what yes / that / it / open / cancel refers to).
- S: about the session, but a successor can answer from the handoff and disk.
- I: stands on its own, or what it needs is on disk.
- A: without the context, the reply could lead to a wrong action.

Sample of 60: H 8 (13.3%, 95% CI 6.9–24.2), S 28, I 24. A 5 (8.3%, CI 3.6–18.1).

All 193 returns: H 19, which is 9.8% of returns, 6.1% of the 310 points and 3.6% of all 528 recycles. That is about 9.5 a week fleet-wide; scaling up from the sample instead gives 12.9 a week. A is 10, about 5 a week.
- The A cases: 'Cancel, please.', 'Cancel the plan for us', 'Yes' x3, 'Proceed with your recommendations.', 'Done', '(Done, continue)', 'Looks good…', and '…on that date'.
- The other H cases: 'Open for us' x4, 'Open the latest sheet', 'show me the three identity options', 'Is it net positive to call vs text?', 'Yes he did use the textbook words', 'Apple bug report as in GitHub issue thread?'.
- 17 of the 19 H and 8 of the 10 A are at points the current practice would not recycle, so nearly all of this risk is new.
- About 45 a week (estimated from the sample) are S prompts: 'Good to close?', '(Checking in)', 'SCQA the outcome', '/explain-decisions', and quoted replies.

3) CLASSIFIER. The brief's rule (v0: reference words, or under 15 words with no path) flags 134 of 193. For H it has precision 0.13 and recall 0.95. In practice it detects 'about the session' (H+S on the sample: precision 0.88, recall 0.97), not 'depends on context'.
- My refined rule v1 (lib.py) scores precision 0.64 and recall 0.64 on the holdout, 0.70 and 0.74 overall. It flags 20 against 19 true H.
- v1 is good enough for a weekly count, not for a gate.

4) COST OF A MISS (estimated; mid weights from sim.py, and a median of 17 later requests that carry the extra context).
- Re-deriving 2.1k tokens (the final message plus about 2k of tool calls) costs 0.0009 pp per miss.
- Re-deriving 58.5k tokens (as much as a whole re-prime) costs 0.021 pp per miss.
